question_text: A piece of metal is subjected to a cyclic stress of 80 MPa. If the phase angle $\delta = 0.1^\circ$ and no heat is transferred to the surroundings, what will be the temperature rise after 100,000 cycles? Data: $E = 80 \text{ GPa}$, $C = 800 \text{ J} / (\text{kg} \cdot \text{K})$, and $\rho = 4.2 \text{ Mg} / \text{m}^3$.The unit of the answer is $ {}^{\circ} C$.
response:
## Reasoning

When a material is cyclically stressed with a phase lag $\delta$ between stress and strain, the stress–strain curve forms a **hysteresis loop**. The area of this loop is the energy dissipated (as heat) per unit volume per cycle:

$$\Delta u = \frac{\pi \sigma^{2}}{E}\sin\delta$$

For small $\delta$, $\sin\delta \approx \delta$ (in radians).

**Energy per unit volume after $N$ cycles:**

$$u_{\text{tot}} = N\,\frac{\pi \sigma^{2}}{E}\sin\delta$$

Since **no heat escapes to the surroundings**, all dissipated energy raises the temperature:

$$\Delta T = \frac{u_{\text{tot}}}{\rho C} = \frac{N\,\pi \sigma^{2}\sin\delta}{E\,\rho\,C}$$

**Substitution of values:**

| Symbol | Value |
|---|---|
| $\sigma$ | $80\times10^{6}$ Pa |
| $\delta$ | $0.1^{\circ}=1.745\times10^{-3}$ rad |
| $E$ | $80\times10^{9}$ Pa |
| $\rho$ | $4.2\times10^{3}$ kg/m³ |
| $C$ | $800$ J/(kg·K) |
| $N$ | $10^{5}$ |

$$\Delta T = \frac{10^{5}\cdot\pi\cdot(80\times10^{6})^{2}\cdot\sin(0.1^{\circ})}{(80\times10^{9})(4200)(800)} \approx 13.06\;^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$$

$$\boxed{13.06}$$
